ing: ripe or mature, peeled and cored; or green plantains
st: Peel the breadfruit, remove the core, and cut into chunks.
Boil the chunks in water 25 minutes until very soft. Drain well.
Mash to a thick, smooth paste in a bowl. Traditional bwiro is fermented for days, but this home version skips fermenting for safety and speed.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] coconut milk, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water and wipe dry. Spoon the paste onto the leaves.
Fold the leaves into tight parcels and tie them closed or wrap in foil.
Steam the parcels on a rack above [[3 cups]] water for 1 hour 15 minutes, adding water if needed.
Cool, unwrap, and slice. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Rinse [[1.5 cups]] rice until the water runs clear.
Cook with [[3 cups]] water and [[0.25 tsp]] salt: bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 18 minutes.
Rest the rice 10 minutes covered.
Meanwhile, toast [[1.5 cups]] shredded coconut in a dry pan for 3 minutes until lightly golden, then spread on a plate.
Stir [[3 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tbsp]] coconut oil into the warm rice.
Wet your hands and roll the rice into balls about 2 inches wide.
Roll each ball in the toasted coconut until fully coated. Serve at room temperature.
Keep the fish in the fridge until the moment you start. Use only very fresh, sushi-grade fish, and cut it into half-inch cubes.
Squeeze the limes to get [[0.5 cup]] juice.
Put the fish in a glass bowl and pour the lime juice over so it is mostly covered.
Stir in [[0.5 tsp]] salt and refrigerate 15 minutes, turning once, until the outside turns opaque.
Drain off about half the lime juice.
Stir in the onion, chili and cucumber if using, then pour in [[0.5 cup]] chilled coconut milk.
Chill 5 minutes and serve very cold with rice or breadfruit.

ing: mature but firm; or green plantains
st: Peel the breadfruit, remove the core, and cut into pieces.
Slice as thin as possible, about 1 millimeter, using a sharp knife or mandoline.
Soak the slices in [[4 cups]] cold salted water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat very dry with towels.
Heat [[3 cups]] vegetable oil and [[2 tbsp]] coconut oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry a handful of slices at a time, 2 to 3 minutes, until pale golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] sugar if you want a sweet and salty taste.
Cool completely so they crisp up, then eat the same day.

ing: or cooked pandan paste; or mashed sweet potato as a stand-in
st: Peel and chop the pandanus fruit. If using sweet potato as a stand-in, peel and cube it instead.
Boil it in [[3 cups]] water 25 minutes until very soft. Drain well.
Mash to a thick paste in a pot.
Add [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[1 cup]] shredded coconut and [[0.5 cup]] coconut milk.
Cook over low heat 20 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick and dark.
Spread the paste on softened banana leaves in a layer about 1 inch thick and wrap tightly.
Bake at 250°F (120°C) for 1 hour until firm and chewy.
Cool and cut into strips to serve.
